newsitem.title: INDIA: Profiteers hawk coffins after India crash - papers.
newsitem.headline: Profiteers hawk coffins after India crash - papers.

text.p: Profiteers outside a New Delhi hospital demanded that relatives of victims of the worst mid-air collision in aviation history pay exorbitant prices for coffins, Indian newspapers said on Friday.
The newspapers said some relatives were also made to pay to have the bodies of their kin embalmed before authorities intervened and offered to cover that cost.
The coffin salesmen awaited relatives at the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), where some 50 bodies were brought on Thursday from the site of Tuesday's crash in which 349 people died.
All passengers and crew aboard a Saudi Arabia Airlines jumbo jet and a Kazakh Ilyushin Il-76 cargo plane were killed when the planes collided about 80 km (50 miles) west of New Delhi.
The Statesman newspaper said the profiteers were asking 5,700 rupees ($160) for coffins, compared with a normal market price of 1,200 rupees ($35).
"My first encounter at AIIMS was not with doctors but with touts busy booking orders for coffins for 5,700 rupees," the Statesman quoted Mohammad Sammin, a relative of one victim, as saying.
An AIIMS spokesman told the Statesman that the coffin salesmen were permitted.
"This has become an essential service of the hospital for those who need coffins. Otherwise, relatives of the dead have to go to find shops of coffins," he was quoted as saying.
Relatives of several victims were made to pay 4,000 rupees ($110) to have the bodies embalmed. Later, authorities told the hospital that the government would pay for the embalming.

"The airport authorities had told us to go to the AIIMS saying that bodies would be handed over then and thereafter, embalming (would occur)," Habib Siddqui, whose cousin died in the collision, told the Statesman.
"They never said that we should go with 10,000 rupees ($285)," he added.
